newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Male domain of Australian submariner to end.
newsitem.headline: Male domain of Australian submariner to end.

text.p: The exclusively male domain of the Australian submariner is about to surface for the last time, with the Australian navy posting women aboard its submarines.
The Royal Australian Navy said on Wednesday that 83 women would begin shore-based training by January 1998 and would serve on the new locally developed Collins class submarines in 1999.

The diesel-electric Collins class, based on Sweden's Kockums-designed Type 471, are the first submarines with crew quarters considered appropriate for mixed crew, with individual bunks, a navy spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday.
Australia's old submarines saw crews "hot bed" -- the practice of rotating through a small number of bunks.
The Navy spokesman said he could not say if women would remain aboard if the submarine faced combat.

Defence Industry, Science and Personnel Minister Bronwyn Bishop will become the first woman to submerge and spend a night aboard an Australian navy submarine when she sails aboard the first Collins class sub, HMAS Collins, next week.
Australia is building six of the Collins class vessels for delivery by 2000 and may order two more.
